newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nice Mayor to hold referendum on begging ban.
newsitem.headline: Nice Mayor to hold referendum on begging ban.

text.p: - The conservative mayor of the French Riviera capital Nice has decided to hold a referendum to test public support for a ban on begging in the city.

Jacques Peyrat, one of several French mayors to impose the controversial ban this summer, told reporters late on Tuesday that if the city council approved the referendum, Nice residents would go to the polls on November 24.
Peyrat announced in June a ban in the city centre on begging, defecating in public and consuming alcohol in a way likely to trigger brawls.

Since it came into effect, at least 800 homeless people have been rounded up by city police and driven 16 km (10 miles) out of the tourist haven to a municipal hostel in Mont Chauve where they were questioned before being released, lawyers say.
Twenty-one of them have sued the city for violating their rights.
"As far as I'm concerned, the results have been good and we have attained our goal. We should repeat the the operation in 1997," said Peyrat, a member of the ruling Gaullist RPR party.

Human rights organisations have protested against such bans, which have also been adopted in Cannes and Menton on the Riviera, La Rochelle on the Atlantic coast and Pau and Carcassonne in the southwest.
A court suspended them in three other southern cities, ruling that they violated the principle of equality among citizens.
